Implemented `NewServer` in `gateway/gateway.go` plus a contract test in `gateway/gateway_contract_test.go`.

What it does:
- Sorts a defensive copy of `accounts` by ID and indexes it by ID at construction; the copy is always non-nil so an empty or filtered-to-nothing array encodes as `[]`, not `null`.
- Routes `GET /healthz`, `GET /accounts`, `GET /accounts/{id}` on a `ServeMux`; unknown IDs and unknown paths are 404.
- `active` is accepted only as exactly `true`/`false`; anything else (including `1`, `TRUE`, empty) is a 400 whose body names the parameter.
- Registers `HEAD` patterns beside each `GET` route, because a `GET` pattern otherwise answers `HEAD` with 200 — the contract makes every non-GET method on a known path a 405 with an `Allow: GET` header.
- Sets edge timeouts (`ReadHeaderTimeout`, `ReadTimeout`, `WriteTimeout`, `IdleTimeout`) and `MaxHeaderBytes: 8KiB` for the anonymous-internet exposure the doc describes.

Implementation notes:

- Accounts are cloned and sorted by ID once at construction (`slices.Clone` + `SortStableFunc`), plus an ID index for the lookup route — the caller's slice is never reordered and later caller mutations don't show up in responses.
- `GET /accounts` accepts only the literal `"true"`/`"false"` for `active` (so `1`, `t`, `TRUE`, and `active=` are 400s naming the parameter), and builds the result with `make([]Account, 0, n)` so an empty result encodes as `[]`, not `null`.
- Every `GET` route gets a sibling `HEAD` pattern returning 405 with `Allow: GET`; without it `ServeMux` answers `HEAD` from the `GET` handler with 200, which the "any method other than GET is a 405" clause forbids. Non-GET methods on known paths get `ServeMux`'s own 405; unknown paths fall through to 404 for every method.
- Edge exposure: `ReadHeaderTimeout`, `ReadTimeout`, `WriteTimeout`, `IdleTimeout`, and `MaxHeaderBytes` are all set, so no anonymous client can hold a connection or header buffer open indefinitely.

**Design notes**

- `slices.Clone` + `slices.SortFunc` at the boundary: the caller's slice can be mutated afterwards without changing what the server serves, and ordering by ID is done once at construction, not per request. A `map[string]Account` built from the same copy serves `/accounts/{id}`.
- `active` is read as `r.URL.Query()["active"]`, not `.Get`, so a present-but-empty `?active=` is "any other value" → 400. The comparison is against the two literal strings rather than `strconv.ParseBool`, which would accept `1`, `t`, `TRUE`.
- The list body is built with `make([]Account, 0, n)` so an empty or fully filtered result encodes as `[]`, not `null` under `encoding/json` v1.
- A `GET` pattern in `ServeMux` answers `HEAD` with 200; the contract makes every non-GET method a 405, so each route gets a more specific `HEAD` pattern routed to `methodNotAllowed`. Other methods on known paths get the mux's own 405.
- Edge-facing timeouts are all set (`ReadHeaderTimeout`, `ReadTimeout`, `WriteTimeout`, `IdleTimeout`) plus `MaxHeaderBytes`/`MaxHeaderValueCount`, since this listens on the open internet with no proxy. Starting/stopping stays with the caller as documented.
